column1:
The March 17, 2021 FOMC statement remains highly accommodative (policy rate at 0–0.25 percent and ongoing Treasury and agency MBS purchases) to sustain credit flows. SLOOS around this period indicates improving credit conditions: large banks eased standards for GSE-eligible, QM jumbo, and other QM mortgages, and foreign banks reported strengthened demand for C&I loans—evidence that supply and demand for credit were firming alongside policy support. Still, many banks cited concerns about the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and risk tolerance, aligning with lingering pandemic uncertainty and noted market vulnerabilities. Balancing better credit dynamics with these risks, sentiment is modestly positive but guarded, slightly stronger than before.
